skill.name: ir-velociraptor
skill.description: Build Velociraptor incident response workflows, VQL hunts, artifact templates, offline collectors, and deployment guidance for authorized DFIR work.
skill.summary: Guides authorized endpoint forensics and threat hunting with Velociraptor and VQL.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by defensive Velociraptor examples, VQL detection patterns, MITRE terminology, and placeholder configuration. I confirmed risks in the deployment and CI guidance, including remote script execution, privileged service installation, broad network binding, temporary client config handling, webhook secret placement, and insecure NFS guidance. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Remote script execution in CI template
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell installation with pinned releases, checksum verification, or packaged scanner actions.
Pin package versions and GitHub Actions to immutable versions or commit SHAs, then document update procedures.

remediation.issue: Privileged deployment commands and persistent services
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit operator approval, least-privilege service users, rollback steps, and review before enabling services at boot.

remediation.issue: Velociraptor services bound to all interfaces
remediation.suggestion: Bind administrative services to restricted interfaces where possible and enforce firewall, TLS, RBAC, and audit logging controls.
Write client configuration to a restricted directory with owner-only permissions and remove temporary files after packaging.

remediation.issue: Webhook secret shown in a template file
remediation.suggestion: Load webhook URLs from CI or secret-manager variables and avoid committing real webhook values.
Remove no_root_squash, use least-privilege export options, and document storage hardening for shared deployments.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned CI Tool Installation
semantic_findings.description: The CI template installs security tools and actions from mutable package names, branches, or remote scripts. Pin versions, prefer verified actions, and verify release checksums before execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple CI steps install tools without version pins or integrity checks, and one action tracks a mutable branch. The file is a reusable template, so this insecure pattern could be copied into production pipelines.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure NFS Export Option
semantic_findings.description: The deployment guide shows an NFS export using no_root_squash for Velociraptor storage. This can allow remote root access to retain root privileges on the shared export.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The no_root_squash option is present directly in the example export line. This is a well-known NFS hardening issue and is not covered by the static hardcoded-IP pattern.

critical_findings.title: Pipe to shell pattern
critical_findings.confidence_reasoning: The template executes a downloaded shell script with `curl | bash`, which can run arbitrary upstream code in CI. This is a direct supply-chain execution risk.

high_findings.title: Hardcoded URL
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The URL is used as the source for a remote install script that is immediately executed by the CI job. A mutable remote script creates supply-chain risk.

content.value_statement: Incident teams need repeatable endpoint evidence collection without losing scope control. This skill provides Velociraptor workflows, VQL patterns, and deployment checklists for authorized investigations.
actual_capabilities: Plan Velociraptor collection workflows for compromised endpoints.
Draft VQL hunt logic for suspicious processes, network activity, persistence, and timelines.
Guide custom artifact design with parameters, preconditions, and reporting notes.
Prepare offline collector and enterprise deployment checklists.
Map Velociraptor detections to MITRE ATT&CK techniques.
limitations: Requires an authorized Velociraptor deployment and access to target endpoints.
Does not verify evidence integrity outside the procedures the user follows.
Does not replace legal approval, privacy review, or chain-of-custody controls.
Some deployment examples need hardening before production use.

use_cases.title: Triage Active Incidents
use_cases.description: Create a scoped plan to collect logs, process data, network activity, persistence artifacts, and timelines from affected endpoints.

use_cases.title: Run Threat Hunts
use_cases.description: Design Velociraptor hunts for suspicious PowerShell, lateral movement, webshells, credential access, and unusual outbound activity.

use_cases.title: Prepare DFIR Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Review server, client, collector, TLS, storage, RBAC, and audit logging plans before deploying Velociraptor.

prompt_templates.title: Start an Investigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Velociraptor triage plan for a suspected compromised Windows workstation. Include scope, artifacts, evidence handling, and first-hour priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Hunt
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Velociraptor hunt for suspicious PowerShell activity across production Windows servers. Include target selection, resource limits, triage fields, and false-positive checks.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Artifact Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me specify a custom Velociraptor artifact for persistence discovery. Define parameters, preconditions, data sources, reporting fields, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Deployment Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this planned Velociraptor enterprise deployment for operational and security risk. Focus on TLS, RBAC, service installation, storage, logging, and rollback.

output_examples.input: Plan initial triage for a suspected ransomware event on five endpoints.
output_examples.output: A phased response plan with endpoint scope, priority artifacts, collection order, evidence handling notes, and escalation criteria.

output_examples.input: Create a hunt for suspicious PowerShell and command shell behavior.
output_examples.output: A hunt design covering target labels, process indicators, command-line patterns, resource limits, review fields, and triage decisions.

output_examples.input: Assess Velociraptor deployment readiness for production.
output_examples.output: A readiness checklist for TLS, RBAC, client rollout, service permissions, storage design, audit logging, backups, and network exposure.

best_practices: Use written authorization, defined scope, and chain-of-custody notes before collecting endpoint evidence.
Test hunts on a small client group before enterprise-wide execution.
Encrypt collections and restrict Velociraptor administrative access with RBAC and audit logging.
anti_patterns: Do not run broad hunts across production without resource limits and rollback planning.
Do not collect credentials, browser data, or personal files without explicit approval.
Do not paste production secrets, certificates, or webhook URLs into shared templates.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps authorized teams plan Velociraptor-based endpoint forensics, threat hunting, artifact development, and deployment reviews.

faq.question: Does it run Velociraptor automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and templates. Users must run tools in their own authorized environment.

faq.question: Can it help write VQL?
faq.answer: Yes. It can outline VQL patterns and artifact designs for common incident response questions.

faq.question: Is it safe for production use?
faq.answer: Use it with review. Some deployment examples need pinning, secret handling, and network hardening before production.

faq.question: What approvals are needed?
faq.answer: Use organizational authorization, privacy review, and legal guidance before collecting endpoint or user data.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
